comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — confirmed; analysis only, no fix applied)

ROOT CAUSE — show's read path never queries incoming edges. `show_state` (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:277) = resolve → `reduce_ticket` → `public_state`, and `reduce_ticket` replays ONLY the subject ticket's own event directory. A LINK event is stored one-sided in the SOURCE ticket's dir (`process_link`, src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:368 appends to state["deps"] at :402), so for `A --blocks--> B` the edge exists solely in A's record: show B renders deps:[] with no trace of A. The data is NOT dropped downstream — it is never fetched. The read-only derivation that answers "who points at me?" already exists (`find_inbound_relationships`, src/rebar/reducer/_inbound.py:75), is exported in the public API (src/rebar/__init__.py:121) and consumed in production by the close gate (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:136) — but no show/list/search path calls it. The NOTE at reads.py:290-293 documents this: the production dispatcher's show arm was never augmented with inbound_links; only a never-dispatched ticket-show.sh shim had the wiring, deleted in commit 28406790c6.

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE (experiments run):
1. Live store: `rebar show eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a` → deps show only OUTGOING (blocks→8625, relates_to→34cd); `rebar show 8625-7bea-67db-4cdc` (open, genuinely blocked) → deps:[] — looks unblocked; but `rebar deps 8625` → blockers:[dc0d…,eb58…,eb6e…], ready_to_work:false. Same CLI, contradictory impressions — reproduces the report exactly.
2. Unit repro (fake store, A --blocks--> B): RAW reduce_ticket(B).deps=[] and no inbound key ever exists on the state (rejects H3 "computed then stripped" — unlike managed_refs, which IS stripped in _cmd_show, nothing inbound is ever computed); find_inbound_relationships(B) on the SAME store returns [{from_id:A, relation:blocks}] (rejects H2 "data absent from store"); show_state(B) contains no mention of A anywhere while find_ready_tickets correctly withholds B (confirms H1 "never queried"). ready's truth comes from a full-corpus edge inversion (`build_blocked_by`, src/rebar/graph/_relations.py:15) that show never consults.

SIBLING SURFACES (named, not filed — all funnel through the same show_state): MCP `show_ticket` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:48 → rebar.show_ticket → src/rebar/_reads.py:53 → show_state) SHARES the defect, as do the library facade `rebar.show_ticket`, the least-privilege agent tool (src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:219), `--output llm`, and list/search (same public_state shape). NOT affected: `rebar deps` / MCP `ticket_deps` (build_dep_graph returns blockers + ready_to_work) and `ready`/`next-batch`.

LEGITIMACY — defect-class (incomplete-implementation). Inbound-in-show was designed and built: the RED test suite is titled "inbound-relationship derivation (ticket show completeness)" (tests/scripts/reducer/test_ticket_inbound.py:1), the llm formatter still carries the inbound_links→ibl mapping (src/rebar/reducer/llm_format.py:50), and the shim contained the exact wiring (state['inbound_links']=…) but was never dispatched — built-but-unwired. Honest counter-citation: commit 28406790c6 dropped that wiring marked "intended, breaking window", and test_reducer_single_source pins the show==list==search shape — but that intent is refactor hygiene (collapse dual read paths, preserve production shape), not a product rationale that blocked-ness should be invisible; no such rationale exists anywhere. The gap causes documented operational failure (this ticket: doomed dispatch of a subagent onto a blocked ticket).

PHASE-2 SKETCH: derive at read time in show_state (no stored mirror, so nothing can drift): compute blocked_by via the SAME build_blocked_by inversion ready uses (single source ⇒ show and ready cannot disagree — AC#5), plus a direction-labeled inbound_links list from find_inbound_relationships (generalises to discovered_from/duplicates; relates_to dedupe already handled by _SYMMETRIC_RELATIONS in _inbound.py). Cost note: find_inbound_relationships byte-scans the corpus — fine per-show, too hot for list N tickets ⇒ scope augmentation to show and deliberately amend the test_reducer_single_source contract (show ⊇ list shape), documenting the decision per AC#4. Extend TicketStateOut so MCP show_ticket surfaces it; llm format reuses the existing ibl mapping.

SUGGESTED RED ORACLE: tmp tracker with A --blocks--> B; assert (1) show_state(B)/`rebar show B --output json` exposes blocker A with unambiguous direction (blocked_by contains A; deps unchanged), (2) same fixture pins show against find_ready_tickets: B absent from ready ⇔ show(B) reports it blocked. Fails today — proven: show_state(B) deps:[] and A appears nowhere in its output.

comments.body: Deferral disposition (epic 2f4c close): CONFIRMED pre-existing read-path defect — show_state never queries incoming edges (RCA in prior comment, src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:277), so blocked-by is invisible on the blocked ticket. NOT a defect in anything epic 2f4c changed or built: the epic's deliverables (gates, detectors, calibration, migrations) neither touch the reads path nor depend on inbound-edge rendering; the epic worked around it operationally via 'rebar list --parent=<id>'. Deferred as its own unit of work with a concrete Phase-2 sketch already on this ticket: invert the existing build_blocked_by index at read time to surface inbound depends_on/blocks edges in show output. Remains open, unclaimed, ready for a plan-review pass by the next agent picking it up.

comments.body: OPERATOR-RATIFIED DECISION (2026-08-04), recorded before implementation: ADDITIVE fix. Render computed INBOUND edges under a NEW key/section (inbound_deps / 'blocked by'), reusing the inbound-blocker computation that 'ready' already performs (build_blocked_by inversion / find_inbound_relationships). Do NOT change existing keys or semantics; the MCP show_ticket outputSchema change must be additive only (update the schema and docs/mcp-reference.md if show's schema is declared there). Implementation proceeding on worktree fix/05cb-inbound-edges under strict TDD (RED behavioral tests first).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PROGRESS: fix implemented on worktree fix/05cb-inbound-edges, pushed as Gerrit change 1367 (Change-Id I7281b9fd8f51ac581dfeb53fbc4f04a105a3aefa, commit 964330d3).

IMPLEMENTATION (additive, per ratified decision): reads.show_state gains include_inbound (default False — gates/field-reads/list/search pay nothing); when set it adds the NEW computed key inbound_deps: sorted [{from_id, relation, status}] entries, each meaning 'from_id <relation> this ticket', derived at read time via the existing find_inbound_relationships (the same derivation the close gate uses) enriched with each source ticket's current status so blocked-ness is readable from a single show. CLI show default view and MCP show_ticket pass include_inbound=True; library rebar.show_ticket exposes the opt-in kwarg. TicketStateOut + ticket_state.schema.json declare the field (additive; rebar.types regenerated); docs updated (ticket-model.md, user-guide.md, mcp-reference.md).

AC#4 DECISION (generalisation) — the fix is GENERAL, not special-cased to blocks: find_inbound_relationships surfaces every stored one-sided relation (blocks, depends_on, discovered_from, duplicates, supersedes, caused_by). Reasoning: the defect is the one-sided STORAGE of LINK events, which affects every directional relation identically; deriving all inbound edges at one seam costs the same corpus scan as blocks alone and keeps direction unambiguous via the uniform 'from_id <relation> this ticket' reading. Reciprocal relates_to entries are deduped by the existing _SYMMETRIC_RELATIONS handling. The --output llm arm is deliberately left inbound-free to preserve the show/list llm parity contract (test_llm_parity_show_vs_list) — recorded as a residual gap.

TDD: 5 behavioral tests seen RED first (KeyError: inbound_deps) in tests/interfaces/queries/test_show_inbound_deps.py — CLI + MCP visibility, unblocked ticket renders [], show-vs-ready pinned on one fixture (cannot disagree, incl. after closing the blocker), discovered_from generalisation. All GREEN after fix; make lint + make typecheck exit 0; touched-area suites green (one pre-existing baseline failure in test_tracker_config_e2e unrelated, fails on clean origin/main too).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar show <id>` renders only the edges STORED ON THAT TICKET'S RECORD. For a `blocks` relation that
is the OUTGOING side. So a ticket that is blocked BY something shows NOTHING about it, and the reader
has to already know which other ticket to inspect in order to discover the blocker.

MEASURED on the live store:

    rebar show eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a  ->  deps [('blocks', '8625-7bea-67db-4cdc')]
    rebar show 0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac  ->  deps [('blocks', 'eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a')]

The real chain is `0d76 --blocks--> eb6e --blocks--> 8625`. But reading eb6e alone, the only visible
edge points DOWNSTREAM, and eb6e looks unblocked.

## The failure this actually caused, today

An agent inspected eb6e, saw only the outgoing edge, and concluded "nothing blocks eb6e — its only dep
is outgoing." On that basis it told the operator the ticket could be planned in parallel, and dispatched
a subagent to decompose and plan-review it. The subagent could never have succeeded: per AGENTS.md,
`review-plan` on a ticket "open but still blocked by an unclosed dependency" FAST-FAILS with no LLM
(unsigned INDETERMINATE, exit 2), and `claim` refuses too. The dispatch was caught and stood down before
it spent anything, but only because a human asked a follow-up question about dependency edges.

The reasoning error was reading one side of a bidirectional relation and concluding from it. The tool
made that the DEFAULT reading: the information needed to answer "is this ticket blocked?" is definitionally
not on the ticket you are looking at.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than learning around

* "Is this blocked?" is one of the most common questions asked of `rebar show`, and it is the one
  question the current output cannot answer.
* It fails toward FALSE CONFIDENCE. The reader does not see an empty or ambiguous field; they see a
  populated `deps` list that looks complete, and reasonably conclude the picture is whole.
* `ready` and `next-batch` know the truth — they correctly withhold a blocked ticket — so the data is
  available; it is only the per-ticket view that omits it. That inconsistency between two tools in the
  same CLI is itself a trap: an agent that cross-checks `show` against `ready` gets contradictory
  impressions and has no obvious reason to trust `ready`.
* Agents are the primary consumers of `rebar show` in this workflow, and they cannot ask a colleague.

## Approach

Render INCOMING edges alongside outgoing ones in the ticket view, clearly labelled by direction — e.g. a
`blocked_by` list derived from the reverse index, so "is this blocked?" is answerable from a single
`rebar show`. Whether that is a new field, a decorated `deps` list, or a derived summary is a design
call; the requirement is that the blocked-ness of a ticket is visible on the ticket.

Consider whether the same asymmetry affects other relations rendered in `deps` (parent/child are already
handled separately via `parent_id`, but `discovered_from`, `duplicates` and `relates_to` have the same
one-sided storage), and whether the fix should be general rather than special-cased to `blocks`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar show <id>` on a ticket blocked by an unclosed dependency makes that blocker visible without
      the reader needing to inspect the blocking ticket.
- [x] A test constructs `A --blocks--> B` and asserts the blocker is discoverable from `show B`, failing
      before the fix.
- [x] The direction of every rendered relation is unambiguous — a reader can tell "blocks" from
      "blocked by" without knowing which record the edge is stored on.
- [x] It is decided and recorded whether the fix generalises to the other one-sided relations
      (`discovered_from`, `duplicates`, `relates_to`) or is scoped to `blocks`, with the reasoning.
- [x] `rebar show` and `ready`/`next-batch` cannot disagree about whether a ticket is blocked; a test
      pins the two against the same fixture.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: rebar show renders only outgoing edges, so blocked-by is invisible on the blocked ticket
